library(PaleoClimR)

## Introduction

PaleoClimR reads HADCM3L NetCDF files formatted by the BRIDGE group. This
vignette demonstrates the package's HADCM3 functions for inspecting grids,
extracting 2D and 3D data, mapping fields, plotting transects, and matching
palaeogeographic occurrence points.

The package includes a reduced HADCM3 example file containing the
`insitu_T_ym_dpth` temperature field and the coordinates needed to interpret
its grid.

```{r example-file}
HADCM3_exp_path <- PaleoClimR.example("HADCM3.permian.example")
HADCM3_file <- "tfkSy_252o.pgclann"
```

## Inspecting grid and NetCDF data

`HADCM3.grid()` returns longitude, latitude, and cell-edge coordinates. With
`dims = 3`, it also returns the model depth levels and depth edges.

```{r grid}
hadcm3_grid <- HADCM3.grid(
  file = HADCM3_file,
  experiment = HADCM3_exp_path,
  dims = 3
)

c(
  longitude_cells = length(hadcm3_grid$lon),
  latitude_cells = length(hadcm3_grid$lat),
  depth_levels = length(hadcm3_grid$depth)
)
```

`HADCM3.get.nc()` reads the requested field and returns it as an array along
with the grid coordinates and time value.

```{r get-netcdf}
temperature_array <- HADCM3.get.nc(
  var = "insitu_T_ym_dpth",
  file = HADCM3_file,
  experiment = HADCM3_exp_path
)

dim(temperature_array$var)
```

## Extracting 2D and 3D data

`HADCM3.data()` extracts one horizontal depth slice and returns a data frame
with cell bounds and a `var` column. In this example, depth level 1 is the
shallowest level.

```{r data-2d}
temperature_surface <- HADCM3.data(
  var = "insitu_T_ym_dpth",
  file = HADCM3_file,
  experiment = HADCM3_exp_path,
  depth.level = 1
)

head(temperature_surface)
```

`HADCM3.data.3D()` returns the field across all model depths, with the depth
midpoint and bounds included for each grid cell.

```{r data-3d}
temperature_3d <- HADCM3.data.3D(
  var = "insitu_T_ym_dpth",
  file = HADCM3_file,
  experiment = HADCM3_exp_path
)

head(temperature_3d)
```

## Mapping HADCM3 fields

`HADCM3.map()` maps a selected depth level. The bundled temperature values are
in degrees Celsius (approximately -1 to 34 °C), so this example displays a
0–40 °C colour range.

```{r map}
HADCM3.map(
  var = "insitu_T_ym_dpth",
  file = HADCM3_file,
  experiment = HADCM3_exp_path,
  depth.level = 1,
  unit.factor = 1,
  min.value = 0,
  max.value = 40,
  intervals = 4,
  scale.label = "Temperature (\u00B0C)"
)
```

## Creating transect plots

`HADCM3.transect()` extracts the nearest latitude or longitude band and plots
the field against depth. With `orientation = "lon"`, `degrees = 0` selects the
latitude band nearest 0° and produces a longitude–depth transect.

```{r transect}
HADCM3.transect(
  var = "insitu_T_ym_dpth",
  file = HADCM3_file,
  experiment = HADCM3_exp_path,
  degrees = 0,
  orientation = "lon",
  continents.outlined = TRUE,
  unit.factor = 1,
  min.value = 0,
  max.value = 40,
  intervals = 4,
  scale.label = "Temperature (\u00B0C)"
)
```

## Matching palaeogeographic points

The bundled `PBDB.permian.example` data include palaeogeographic coordinates
in `p_lng` and `p_lat`. `HADCM3.points.data()` matches occurrences to the
selected HADCM3 field and returns the matched climate value and model grid
coordinates with the original occurrence records.

```{r points-data}
data("PBDB.permian.example", package = "PaleoClimR")

matched_occurrences <- HADCM3.points.data(
  var = "insitu_T_ym_dpth",
  file = HADCM3_file,
  experiment = HADCM3_exp_path,
  depth.level = 1,
  coord.dat = PBDB.permian.example
)

head(matched_occurrences[, c(
  "p_lng", "p_lat", "matched_climate", "lat.bin.mid", "lon.bin.mid"
)])
```

`HADCM3.points.map()` overlays those matched records on the map. The example
uses phylum for a separate categorical point-colour scale; omit `points.col`
to colour points using their matched temperature instead.

```{r points-map}
HADCM3.points.map(
  var = "insitu_T_ym_dpth",
  file = HADCM3_file,
  experiment = HADCM3_exp_path,
  depth.level = 1,
  coord.dat = PBDB.permian.example,
  unit.factor = 1,
  min.value = 0,
  max.value = 40,
  intervals = 4,
  scale.label = "Temperature (\u00B0C)",
  points.col = "phylum",
  points.scale.type = "categorical",
  points.scale.label = "Phylum"
)
```

## Summary

The main HADCM3 workflow is to identify a file and experiment directory,
inspect the grid with `HADCM3.grid()`, extract data with `HADCM3.data()` or
`HADCM3.data.3D()`, and visualize it with `HADCM3.map()` or
`HADCM3.transect()`. Use the point functions to associate palaeogeographic
occurrences with model values and plot the matched records.
